claims.text: Increasing atomic size mismatch in refractory FCC HEA nanoparticles induces localized lattice strain.
Localized lattice strain lowers the energetic barrier for surface-atom mobility.
Lower barriers for surface-atom mobility cause premelting to begin earlier.
Ni–Co–Fe–Cr–Mn is presented as an example of a refractory FCC HEA system.
The proposed nanoparticles have a uniform elemental distribution before heating.
Changing composition while holding the number of elements constant can produce series with different atomic size mismatch.
Differences in constituent atomic radii produce local lattice strains and distortions.
Strain facilitates atomic vibrations and mobility at surfaces and grain boundaries.
Nanoparticles with greater atomic size mismatch will have a lower surface-premelting onset temperature than the minimal-mismatch baseline.
Earlier premelting will manifest as earlier surface disorder and liquid-like atomic motion.
The mismatch-dependent premelting behavior will hold across nanoparticle sizes from 5 to 20 nm.
Nanoparticles made from elements with similar atomic radii have minimal lattice strain.
The minimal-mismatch baseline has a premelting onset close to the expected bulk melting temperature.
The proposed relationship applies specifically to refractory FCC HEA nanoparticles between 5 and 20 nm under inert-atmosphere heating up to 1500 K.
Surface segregation and compositional fluctuations may also affect premelting behavior.
High-resolution strain mapping or atom-probe tomography can help distinguish size-mismatch effects from compositional confounders.

contradictions.description: The system is repeatedly described as a refractory FCC HEA, but Ni–Co–Fe–Cr–Mn is supplied as the representative example without explaining how it meets the stated refractory classification, creating an internal material-class mismatch.
